title: The 4 Preconditions That Decide If Your AI Build Survives
subtitle: A pre-build diagnostic for service-business owners at 11-100 employees who are about to spend $10k+ on automation and don't want it to die in 90 days.

sections.title: Structured Input — Can An Agent Actually Read Your Data?
sections.description: If your intake is free-text garbage, the agent breaks on day one. This section finds the leaks before you build.

items.text: Pull every intake form your business uses and count the optional free-text fields
items.tip: If more than 30% of fields are optional free-text, your agent is going to hallucinate scope. Tighten the form in HubSpot or Typeform first.

items.text: List every place client knowledge lives (Slack, Drive, Notion, CRM, that one spreadsheet on the ops lead's laptop)
items.tip: If the count is higher than 3, your agent will be blind to most of the answer. Consolidate into Notion or Supabase before connecting AI.

items.text: Check that the same field is named the same thing across systems (client_name vs Client Name vs customer)
items.tip: Fuzzy matching costs you weeks. Standardize keys in your source-of-truth table first.

items.text: Write down what happens when an upstream field is missing today (who fixes it, in what tool, how often)

sections.title: Documentable Decision Logic — Can You Encode How Your Best Person Decides?
sections.description: Tacit knowledge has to become explicit rules before an agent can replicate it. Most teams skip this and wonder why the output feels off.

items.text: Ask your two best people to write down lead qualification criteria separately, then compare answers
items.tip: If the two lists don't overlap by at least 70%, you have a process problem wearing an AI costume. Resolve it before you build.

items.text: Document the 5 most common decision points in the workflow you want to automate (with the if/then logic)
items.tip: Use a simple Google Doc or a ClickUp page. If you can't write it down, you can't ship it.

items.text: Have ops log every edge case they handle for one full week
items.tip: Expect 10-15 per week on a workflow leadership thinks is '5 clean steps'. That gap is where automation projects die.

items.text: Flag every decision that currently relies on 'I just know' from one specific person

sections.title: Narrow Initial Scope — Are You Trying To Boil The Ocean?
sections.description: Agents that try to handle every case on day one break on case #3. Pick the 80% predictable work and route the rest.

items.text: Estimate what percentage of cases follow the predictable happy path (look at last 30 days of work in ClickUp or your PM tool)
items.tip: Target the 70-85% predictable slice for v1. Anything below 60% means the process isn't ready for an agent yet.

items.text: Write the explicit list of cases your v1 will NOT handle (and where they route instead)
items.tip: If you can't name what you're cutting, you haven't narrowed the scope. You've just renamed the whole problem.

items.text: Calculate hours-saved-per-week × loaded labor cost × 12 weeks vs. build cost
items.tip: Apply the 90-Day Payback Rule. If the math doesn't return the build cost in 90 days, scope it down or kill it.

items.text: Pick ONE workflow for the first build (not three, not the whole department)

sections.title: Human-In-The-Loop — Did You Design The Review Step On Day One?
sections.description: Every shipped agent routes 15-20% of cases to human review. That's the design working, not the design failing.

items.text: Define the confidence threshold or trigger condition that routes a case to human review
items.tip: In n8n or Make, this is usually an IF node after the LLM call checking confidence_score or a specific output field.

items.text: Name the specific person who owns the review queue and how they get notified
items.tip: Slack DM, ClickUp task, or email. Pick one. Reviews that go to a shared inbox become reviews that don't happen.

items.text: Set up a way for the reviewer's corrections to feed back into the prompt or rules
items.tip: A Supabase table logging overrides + reasons gives you the data to tighten the agent every 2 weeks.

items.text: Document the kill switch — how you pause the agent in under 60 seconds if it goes sideways

completion_cta.headline: Want me to look at your top 3 gaps?
completion_cta.description: Reply to the follow-up email with your answers and I'll send back a 1-page Agent-Ready Blueprint showing which gap to close first and what the build looks like. No call required.
